sense: for each: a head, a day

terms.grammar: preposition with the accusative, often with singulī
evidence: Cic. Font. 9: quaternōs dēnāriōs in singulās vīnī amphorās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “So much a head” is in capita or in singulōs. The amount is often a distributive numeral (singulī, bīnī, ternī, quaternī): trecēnōs … in capita, three hundred a head.

terms.gloss: a, per (twice a day, three times a year)
terms.grammar: preposition with the ablative, after a numeral adverb
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.100: bis in diē saturum fierī
Cic. Rosc. Am. 132: vix ter in annō
terms.comment: semel, bis, ter in diē. “Every day” is cotīdiē, “every year” quotannīs (see every year); for “per cent”, see percent.

phrases.latin: extulit eum plēbs sextantibus conlātīs in capita
phrases.english: the people gave him his funeral, putting in a sixth of an as a head

phrases.latin: pretium fore in capita equitī quīngēnōs quadrīgātōs nummōs, trecēnōs peditī, servō centēnōs
phrases.english: the price would be, per head, five hundred silver pieces for a horseman, three hundred for a foot soldier, a hundred for a slave

phrases.latin: vīta illa beāta, quae ferēbātur, plēna Ītalicārum Syrācūsiārumque mēnsārum, nūllō modō mihi placuit, bis in diē saturum fierī
phrases.english: that “happy life”, as they called it, full of Italian and Syracusan feasting, did not please me at all: to be stuffed full twice a day

phrases.latin: quī in Sallentīnīs aut in Bruttiīs habent unde vix ter in annō audīre nūntium possunt
phrases.english: who have estates among the Sallentini or in Bruttium, from where they can hear news barely three times a year
